import pytest

from your_module import parse_csv_line   # ← adapt as needed


# ---------- Happy-path -------------------------------------------------------

@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "line, expected",
    [
        ("a,b,c", ["a", "b", "c"]),                              # plain CSV
        ('"a,b",c', ["a,b", "c"]),                               # quoted field containing a comma
        ('first,"second, still second","third, too",four',
         ["first", "second, still second", "third, too", "four"]),
        ('"embedded ""quotes"" here",x',
         ['embedded ""quotes"" here', "x"]),                     # doubled quotes stay untouched
    ],
)
def test_parse_csv_line_happy(line, expected):
    assert parse_csv_line(line) == expected


# ---------- Edge cases -------------------------------------------------------

@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "line, expected",
    [
        ("", [""]),                          # completely empty line
        (",", ["", ""]),                     # only a delimiter
        (",a", ["", "a"]),                   # leading comma
        ("a,", ["a", ""]),                   # trailing comma
        ("a,,b,,", ["a", "", "b", "", ""]),  # consecutive commas
        ('""', [""]),                        # empty quoted field
        ('"ab,c', ["ab,c"]),                 # unmatched opening quote
        ('"multi\nline",x', ["multi\nline", "x"]),  # newline inside quotes
    ],
)
def test_parse_csv_line_edge_cases(line, expected):
    assert parse_csv_line(line) == expected


# ---------- Error cases ------------------------------------------------------

@pytest.mark.parametrize("bad_input", [123, 12.34, None, [], {}])
def test_parse_csv_line_type_errors(bad_input):
    """
    The implementation expects an iterable of characters (i.e. a string);
    anything else should raise TypeError because the `for c in line:` loop
    will not be able to iterate over a non-string scalar or non-iterable.
    """
    with pytest.raises(TypeError):
        parse_csv_line(bad_input)
